notes.title: Per Aspera is now available in VR!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/268fa9153d9d62ca1c28e9e4d7bb806be0788ed4.png[/img]

[url=https://www.oculus.com/experiences/quest/7365196930219982/]Per Aspera VR is now available on the Meta VR store![/url] We're so excited to be able to bring a new Per Aspera experience to those that play on the Meta Quest 2 system. We've worked during the last year adapting our game from the ground up for VR alongside our DLC updates for the PC version that you already love. The VR development process has also given us lots of valuable insights that have directly contributed to performance improvements in the PC version that we have been deploying in the last updates.

[b]What is included in the VR version?[/b]
- 6-8 hours of campaign content including VO, narrative, and adapted gameplay.
- A new general balance to accommodate shorter gameplay sessions.
- Some features were simplified or removed in order to make the version as comfortable as possible.
- The ability to get close to the surface of Mars. This will be the closest you can get to Mars without a rocket!

[b]Is Per Aspera VR coming to Steam VR?[/b]
Per Aspera VR is an experience tailored for Meta Quest 2, we are considering what would make sense for PC users and your expectations. That's all we can share for now. We'll update you right here on Steam as soon as any information is available.


Per Aspera, Ad Astra!
- Tlön Industries team

notes.title: Planetary city builder Per Aspera multiplayer is here
notes.content:
There's nothing better than a city-builder game unless it's about building cities on Mars - and you can now do it in co-op, thanks to the newly-added Per Aspera multiplayer modes. As of now, up to four players can work together to colonise Mars, as Per Aspera is now a co-op game.

For the last few months, developer Tlön Industries has held various online betas for players to test out. Now, around 15 months after Per Aspera launched on Steam, the full multiplayer co-op experience is finally available for the sci-fi management game. It works like the Sandbox mode, and there won't be any PvP or military buildings - not yet, anyway.

Basically, how multiplayer in Per Aspera works is that up to four players can land separately on Mars and create their own little districts and colonies. However, research is shared and resources will have to be, too. You can save and return to the session at any point, so you don't have to play a round of this gigantic city builder all at once.

notes.title: TERRAFORM TOGETHER
notes.content:
[b]Multiplayer Launches into Space![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/714e3eb322a54ba2234819a34c5909d321749308.png[/img]

Now you are able to build, modify and terraform Mars with your friends. If you’ve ever thought you needed more hands to make an impact on the big red rock, now is the time to share the experience with your friends (up to 4 players).

[b]Gather your Crew[/b]

The Multiplayer Mode is meant to work as a cooperative experience. Rally your friends and get your hands dirty while building the new landscape. Perform scientific research to enable plant and animal life in an otherwise inhospitable world. Show kindness and cooperation by sharing resources and impactful experiences.
Multiplayer Mode works like the Sandbox experience, so there won’t be any PvP and military buildings. Please note that multiplayer won’t support mods.

[b]Lobbying for Mars[/b]

Lobbies are accessed directly from the Main Menu. From there you can choose to create or join other players in jolly cooperation. Lobbies can be public, where anyone can join you, or private, where only the most privileged of your friends are allowed to take this cosmic endeavor with you. Finally choose the game’s difficulty and start this amazing journey.

[b]Resume Transmission[/b]

Multiplayer games can be saved and continued whenever you want, so don’t worry if it’s getting too late to deploy a new Organic Disposal Plant. All of you will be able to finish your monumental achievement tomorrow.

[b]Everyone, Everywhere all at Once[/b]

Now we’ve also added support for Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Japanese, Russian and Simplified Chinese for the whole multiplayer experience. It’s time to call your friend on the other side of the world and take over a whole new planet!

If you have enjoyed the game and the continuous updates, we kindly ask if you leave us a review. We would very much appreciate it.

[url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/803050/announcements/detail/3127191960112704074]Patch Notes can be found in this separate News.[/url]

[h1]How do I participate?[/h1]

For this Beta, we have decided to keep things simple - If you are playing on the default branch you will be participating and see a new button in the main menu.
On Mars, Betas will come to you willingly!
The Beta will run for approximately 2 Weeks.

[h1]Online Co-Op Basics[/h1]

In Online Co-Op, you and up to three fellow Artificial Consciousnesses can tackle the Terraforming of Mars together in [b]Sandbox Mode[/b].
Mods do [b]not[/b] work in Online Co-Op.
There is no PvP, only Co-Op.

[h2]Gameplay-specifics[/h2]

Each player will receive a landing site they can freely place anywhere on Mars. The Sectors they are placed in will be automatically unlocked.
In Online Co-Op, the Building Limit is adjusted so both players can build complete colonies.
Research is shared between players.
Resources behave like normal. Each Landing Site is its own District, and District rules apply. the Resource numbers shown reflect [b]all[/b] of Mars, not just your lander!

[h2]How to play[/h2]

Playing together is pretty simple!
One of you has to open up a Lobby, as shown in the GIF below. Make sure to set your Room Type appropriately, leaving the Lobby open may allow other players to enter the Room.
When joining, you simply click "Join Lobby" and select the Lobby you want to join for Public ones, or ask your friend to invite you via Steam for Private ones.
You can also continue older games by clicking "Resume Game". Terraform Mars together - At [b]your[/b] pace!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/c035c98cef19ea82a00e144dc3b22da2d5376945.gif[/img]

[h1]I/We found a Bug or another Issue[/h1]

Online Co-Op is currently in a Beta stage, so its expected there might still be some bugs lurking about, but fret not!
Let us know about the Issue you encountered [url=https://rawfury.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/1/group/1/create/18]via this Report Form![/url] We might not reply to every Ticket directly, but we read them all, promise! notes.title: Mars city builder Per Aspera gets new patch and an expansion next year
notes.content:
Sci-fi city-building game Per Aspera is celebrating its first anniversary with a new update and a tease for another expansion coming early next year. There have been five major patches since the Mars colony management game launched last December, as well as the free Green Mars expansion that accompanied the most recent 1.5 update.

Today's 1.5.2 patch brings some extra quality-of-life features, such as changes to resource scattering so that there are now a guaranteed number of each resource in a sector. There's a new easier difficulty option called 'Story' for campaign mode, and 'Playground' for the sandbox mode, with other levels apart from the hardest option getting renamed.

In addition to today's patch, a beta for the next major revision - 1.6 - will hit Steam on December 16 and run through to December 23. This should include the first version of a multiplayer mode. "This is a very big system," developer Tlön Industries explains, "so we do not quite know yet when the update [will be] truly ready as a lot of fine-tuning, fixing, and potentially support systems are still required. This will just be a first look, to collect your feedback, test the systems, and see what we need to refine still."

notes.title: One Year of Per Aspera!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/5d354ec92f6495b412ae61ad39c7566b119198b7.jpg[/img]

[h1]Happy Birthday to Per Aspera![/h1]
Can you believe it has been a [b]whole year[/b]* already? Goodness, time surely flies when you are terraforming! Per Aspera is our first game as a company, and a labor of love that we have been working on for years, and we have not been slacking off since release, having kept busy reading reports, listening to feedback and updating the game accordingly.
We have implemented lots of patches, [b]four[/b] major content updates, a free DLC, countless hotfixes in order to address critical issues, add new buildings and features you have requested and suggested, and just generally improved the game.

If you have not picked the game up in a while, it might be a good time to try again. It will look and feel different, and hopefully much better to play. Explore Mars, and make it your own!

[i]* equals 0.53 martian years.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/2446e1b1dcf9bedd3ac7efa5ff8ba5c02ffd792a.gif[/img]

[h2]Thank [b]you[/b][/h2]
Here at Tlön Industries, we are thankful for the incredible opportunity to create the game of our dreams for players like you. We hope you enjoy this incredible journey as much as we do, and we promise you it is not over yet, and there's still fuel in our tanks!
Before we talk about what's in the future, though, let us recap what has happened since Release.

[h2]Release 1.0[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/51f52be735e0a3605fc160d58c594bba89c620dd.png[/img]
[b]December 3rd, 2020[/b]

The journey begins in earnest. Terraform and colonize Mars. We released 5 Patches for this version of the game, and were nominated for the DICE Game Of The Year award.

[h2]First Content Update: [b]Treat That Water[/b] - 1.1[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/b95f7648b3134abf36f5cf79dfe362e9be4172c7.png[/img]
[b]February 11th, 2021[/b]

A little over two months after the release of Per Aspera, we deployed the first major Content Update. For the most part, [i]Treat That Water[/i] was a Quality Of Life update, improving on our Lenses, Hyperloop UX improvements and the like.
It also brought the [b]Water Treatment Plant[/b], which was highly requested in order to be able to make use of all that water you put on Mars. After all, why not make use of it instead of drilling for Ice, right!?

We released just one Patch for this version of the game.

[h2]Second Content Update: [b]Improved Logistics[/b] - 1.2[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/18417af41ce00d834badbf611a361328f6ace7c0.png[/img]
[b]April 3rd, 2021[/b]

A month after 1.1, and four months after the initial release, we released the second Content Update, [i]Improved Logistics[/i]. Once again, mainly Quality Of Life, allowing you to upgrade roads faster and more efficiently, overhauling storage centers and a general UX pass on everything Production and Logistics.
We were nominated for three awards in the BIG Festival:
[list][*] Best International Game (Finalist)
[*] Best Gameplay (Finalist)
[*] Best Latin American Game (Winner)

We did not release any Patches for this Update.

[h2]Third Content Update: [b]District Planner[/b] - 1.3[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/8c74033a4847c2c26c91578bc45ceeffd27c7880.png[/img]
[b]May 26th, 2021[/b]

For our third Content Update, [i]District Planner[/i], we brought on a handful of new features. The biggest one being the District System which the Update is named for. District let you break down your efforts by allowing you to visualize the resources of each district, which are based on Landing Sites, on its own, finally ending the age old question of [i]Is this piece of Silicone anywhere close to my Glass Kiln, or is it on the other side of the planet with no way for me to access it?[/i]
Also new in this Update was the Terraforming screen, giving you a better visualization for your road to terraforming Mars. Lastly, we improved resource veins by giving them a contextual Build Menu, as well adding [b]Deep[/b] and [b]Ultra-deep[/b] Veins with higher resource yields, while requiring higher tiers of miners.

We released one hotfix for this Update.

[h2]Fourth Content Update: [b]Martian Modding[/b] - 1.4[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/04a072f1c46d96aff82fc43d63602a9ffb590242.png[/img]
[b]July 9th, 2021[/b]

The Modding Update! Create the Mars of your dreams like never before! This Content Update was all about giving you the tools to design new quests, create new resources, or buildings, to modify the Tech Tree, and even modify planet variables!
If you haven't yet, check out the Workshop and start making your own Mods after reading our [url=http://per-aspera.vg/files/Modding%20v1.5%20-%20Green%20Mars.pdf]Modding Operational Instructions here![/url]

We released two Patches for this update.

[h2]First (Free) DLC: [b]Green Mars[/b] - 1.5[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/9274022bca5b9aa46a33b2ed55fc154b2767d5ff.jpg[/img]
[b]October 21st, 2021[/b]

Our first really big Update. Green Mars is all about terraforming, and turning the red ball into a lush green ball. We made major updates to our Water Simulation, in order to render how rivers displace into valleys and craters. We added 11 Biomes for Terraforming, with each one having specific requirement to dictate the growth of both Flora and Fauna.
Similar to the Water Treatment Plant in [i]Treat That Water[/i], we wanted to give you some additional choices to get food in [i]Green Mars[/i], so we added Farms to the game, which require running water.
Did we mention there can be [b]Capybaras[/b] on Mars!?

In the newest update to [i]Green Mars[/i], Version 1.5.2, we are adding new, easier difficulty options, and make Changes to Resource Scattering, to guarantee some of every resource in every sector among some other things.
[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/803050/view/3136191005471550153]Check out the Patch logs here.[/url]

[hr][/hr]

[h1]What's coming next?[/h1]
We are glad you asked! We are not done with Per Aspera yet by a long shot, so let's talk about all the great stuff that's coming!
There is our next, upcoming Content Update, Version 1.6, which will head into an open Beta from December 16th until December 22nd or 23rd. We have had [b]a lot[/b] of requests for this, so we hope you will enjoy this upcoming content. Stay tuned for more Info closer to the 16th!

If you pay attention to the advanced branch patch notes, you'll already know everything in here. We just thought it might be good to repost for the default branch crowd.

[h3]New difficulty options[/h3]
To open Per Aspera up for even more players, we have added a new, easier, difficulty level to both the campaign and the Sandbox mode.

We also took the liberty to rename all difficulty levels to better fit with the game's theme.
The new difficulty option is called [i]Story[/i] for campaign mode, and [i]Playground[/i] for sandbox mode. They are intended for players who want to experience the game without challenges.
Our old difficulty options have gotten glow-ups as well:
[b]Easy[/b] is now called Simulation. Think of it as AMI's training grounds.

We partially reworked how resource nodes are generated. The most significant change being that we now have a guaranteed number of each resource in every sector as opposed to the random-only distribution so far. Two weeks ago, we released the Green Mars free DLC, and with your help we have already been able to pinpoint and squash some bugs, as well as make improvements to various elements of the game, to better reflect the interplay of certain new features in Green Mars with features from the base game.
As usual, we will push the update to the Advanced branch first and will promote it the the default branch after a few days of testing.


The following changes are live for users on the Advanced Branch:

[b]Improvements[/b]
[list]
[*] Updated Flora and Delta O2 Widgets 
[*] Updated C02 Widget to reflect consequences with the Fauna 
[*] Shows Green Mars DLC in the New Game Screen
[*] Shows Terraforming Widgets even after completing Stage 5
[*] Knowledge Base now shows a lot more information for structures, projects, and other entries
[/list]
[b]Bug Fixes[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed issue with Time Slider not capturing clicks correctly 
[*] Fixed issue that after [spoiler]swap[/spoiler] the knowledge base only showed some of the structures
[*] Fixed issue that wouldn't grant new structures pushed by datamodel changes on a previously started savegame 
[*] Fixed call buttons appearing when entering a dialogue or during one
[*] Fixed issue with horses being flipped when viewed from the north 
[*] Fixed issue with a Fauna distribution (rendering)
[*] Fixed typos and localization issues
[*] Fixed issue that would have Dumpsters start with logs already inside the Crater 
[*] [Balance] Fixed issue where Superior Colonies costed more than it should 
[*] Fixed issue that wouldn't update the in-game date on rewritten savegames
[*] Fixed graphics issue with the Delta-02 graphs
[*] Updated Internationalization texts for Green Mars Update 
[*] Lenses stay [b]ON[/b] during special project's camera lock animation
[*] Minor representation fixes for the Terraforming Screen
[*] Fixed issues where the hot key opens the tech-tree but doesn't close it
[*] Fixed issue where the [spoiler]military[/spoiler] drone factory had the wrong output 
[/list]

[h2]How do I access the Advanced branch?[/h2]

Our [b]Advanced branch[/b] is where we push out patches for further testing before launching it to the entire playerbase. As we approach and solve more complicated issues and tweak integral features for balancing, we need time and testing to ensure our public build remains stable. Using the Advanced branch gives you the flexibility to try out these new changes while also giving us time to assess the impact of our new updates! Once we’re assured that the patch is working as intended, we’ll publish it to the public branch of the game, where it will be accessible for all of our players.

[b]How to access the Advanced branch[/b]
If you’re interested in trying out these new changes, then you’ll need to switch over to the proper branch. Changing a branch is simple and easy!

[olist]
[*] Find “Per Aspera” in your Steam Library and access its properties by right clicking and selecting “Properties”.
[*] Navigate to the “Betas” sub-menu.
[*] In the drop-down menu, select the “Advanced” branch.
[*] That’s it! Your game should begin downloading the new patch.
[/olist]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/a8281d903da870b2cfaca4de2826ad93b79d5631.gif[/img]

If you’d ever like to return to the Public branch, simple select “None” under the submenu and Steam will handle the rest!

Ad Astra,
Tlön Industries

Keep in mind that as this is our beta branch, we cannot guarantee that mods you develop, download, or use will remain functional in future updates.

Mod support functionality is [b]currently limited to only the Advanced Branch.[/b] Why? We use this testing branch to make sure our main branch remains stable and functional. Game development is tricky - new updates can have all sorts of unintended consequences - so this test branch lets us see the affects of our upcoming changes. 

Without further ado, here is our [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/803050/workshop/]brand new, shiny workshop![/url]

notes.title: Post Launch Retrospective
notes.content:
[h1]It's our six month anniversary! 🎉[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/2d20265e2e5d7575f8382240d06206119109e923.png[/img]

Six months ago today we welcomed our first players to their new homes on Mars. This game was our first as a new company and a labor of love that took us many years. It's hard to believe that it's been six months since we released Per Aspera to the rest of the world! It's been amazing to see everyone share screenshots and videos of their colonies and watch as you explore Mars and make it your own. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/346e4101ab89de4096a3549c11e2ef6c16abc18c.gif[/img]

Our jobs don't stop at launch, though. Since release we've been listening to your feedback, reading your reports, and slowly but surely updating the game. In our six months together we've implemented patches, content updates, and hotfixes to address critical bugs, add new buildings and features you've requested, and improve the game. 

If you haven't picked up the game in some time, it will probably look a little different and feel much better to play. In this video, we take a moment to share a few of our proudest additions to the game - take a look. There's never been a better time to return back home to Mars!

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cuWhoNsz8Hg

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/08655caf15e272cda35063207193d81bd415aecc.gif[/img]
[h2]If you've played Per Aspera, please leave us a review[/h2]

The importance of reviews for a game like ours and a studio like ours cannot be overstated. That's why we're asking a small favor: if you've played Per Aspera, please take a moment to leave us a Steam review! While we can't respond to all of the reviews be assured that the team reads each and every one of them. The community's aggregate feedback, including reviews, guides our future and allows us to plan new updates to make this game the best it can be. 

[h2]Thank [b]you[/b][/h2]

All of us at Tlön Industries are thankful to have the incredible opportunity to create the game of our dreams for players like you. Thank you for going on this journey to Mars with us. Whether you were here from our first reveal, came to us on launch day, or joined us after a new update... [b]thank you![/b] 

We still have more exciting updates in store for everyone, including mod support, but for now let's look at some of our favorite new features from the past three content updates.

[h2]Content Update #3: District Planner[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/cbfd352cb00fe9d9344918c544bb03e58dbcc5d7.png[/img]

Our latest and largest content update yet is the District Planner update! This update includes nearly a hundred bug fixes, QOL improvements, and plenty of new features including:
[list]
[*] [b]Districts:[/b] The new Districts Lens allows you to visualize the resources of each individual district separately. You can turn on/off the "District Boundary" that each Landing Site emanates. Each district has a different name that you can customize.
[*][b]Terraforming Screen:[/b] The new terraforming screen provides a roadmap of the overall terraforming plan.
[*][b]Deep & Ultra-deep Veins:[/b] We added new types of veins with much higher quantities. Deep and Ultra-deep veins require higher tiers of Mines.
[*][b]Advanced Landing Site:[/b] Players can now research and deploy Advanced Landing Sites, which provide even more resources and power to help expand the base.
[*] [b]Easier Mine Construction:[/b] New contextual Build Menu when clicking on Veins.
[/list]
Read all of the patch notes here:
https://steamcommunity.com/games/803050/announcements/detail/3053982465478603349

[h2]Content Update #2: Improved Logistics[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/6d2e9538de9768aa828bacc9788c6734f7d84fc0.png[/img]
[list]
[*] [b]Group Selection & Upgrading:[/b] You can select and upgrade multiple ways at the same time.
[*] [b]Improved Storage[/b]General overhaul of storage center functionality.
[*] [b]Updated Workers Widget:[/b] it will now notify players if production becomes unsustainable and if you need to start producing more workers!
[*] [b]Sparklines:[/b] Added Sparklines to all productions to quickly alert players of resource stockpiles or depletions.
[/list]
Our Improved Logistics content update introduced many more fixes and QOL improvements! Check out the patch notes here:
https://steamcommunity.com/games/803050/announcements/detail/3017949229475577091

[h2]Content Update #1: Treat That Water[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/b95f7648b3134abf36f5cf79dfe362e9be4172c7.png[/img]
[list]
[*] [b]New Water Treatment Plant:[/b] A new building that lets you collect water for your colonists from Martian oceans!
[*][b]Updated Lenses:[/b] An overhaul to the lenses that makes it easier to parse your colony's data!
[*][b]Coordinates:[/b] A new feature that lets you see positional information for key places.
[*][b]Informational Prompts:[/b] We added pop-ups during key moments of the game to teach and inform about new mechanics.
[/list]
This first patch introduced a lot of fixes for frustrating bugs as well as pivotal quality of life improvements. Read the full patch notes for the Treat That Water update:
https://steamcommunity.com/games/803050/announcements/detail/5825939260223890653

notes.title: Welcome home to Mars: play our free demo until May 9th!

[h2]Get a taste of life on Mars[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/8124f65a2aaa1dfc72ee487df0c8413b9f5a51f8.gif[/img]

Welcome to your new home: Mars. Per Aspera is a planet-sized city-builder where you take control of the world's most sophisticated AI and build humanity's new home. Succeed where all others have failed and transform the barren Red Planet into a verdant paradise.

To celebrate our inclusion in the BIG Festival, we'll be offering a [b]free demo until May 9th![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/95ad2726245e52c6f37a146ce3566edcceefdb96.gif[/img]

Get a small taste of life on the Red Planet with our free demo. Begin the journey to terraform Mars, meet your maker Dr. Foster, and bring your first colonists to their new home. The demo gives you a taste of the resource management, compelling narrative, and planet building experience: explore your new home in the free demo until [b]May 9th.[/b]

Per Aspera is 20% off until May 1st as part of LudoNarraCon, a digital celebration of narrative indie games like ours. 

[h2]We're in the BIG Festival![/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/0fb238cf07676718e5caf9ec0b2d7f9239f69d42.png[/img]

The BIG Festival begins May 3rd and lasts until May 9th - a week long celebration of indie games! Learn more about [url=https://www.bigfestival.com.br/homeen.html]Brazil's Independent Games Festival here.[/url]

Experience a building simulator at a massive scale like never before. Explore a new frontier: the entire planet of Mars is yours to cultivate! Grow your humble landing site into a planet-wide urban sprawl with a legion of workers and drones to command. With the planet as your canvas, the possibilities are endless.

notes.title: The future of Per Aspera: our development roadmap
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/29a62f29a12dc9f7c5f15ea5cd403e65bd1ab207.png[/img]

Since the release of Per Aspera, we've deployed regular patches and our first content update! We don't plan on stopping there, either. We have a lot in store for the game and decided it's time to share with our players a little more about where we're going. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/bb55f6a5c8190f4b42ec24ba4646f41a7441f736.png[/img]

This roadmap encompasses the larger content updates that are planned and in development. To give you a sense of scale and scope, these updates will be similar in impact and size as our [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/803050/announcements/detail/5825939260223890653]v1.1 Treat That Water content update.[/url]

Our next content updates are planned to be released throughout the year during the second and third quarters. As we come closer to releasing a new content update, we'll deploy changes to our Advanced Branch to ensure build stability. Our [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/803050/announcements/detail/4544662635990811383]Advanced Branch[/url] is where we test new changes and assess how our newest updates impact the rest of the game. Once we're happy with the performance & integrity of the build, we'll push the new content update onto our public branch and announce it on Steam for everyone!

As you can see, our next content update, named [b]Nuts & Bolts: Improved Logistics[/b] will be launching soon...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/ee76dc4675f75e0bacde168d217d40057e84b42b.png[/img]

We're excited to announce that our next content update will be releasing this month in late March! Since that's fairly soon, we're happy to reveal what this update contains. Our [b]Nuts & Bolts: Improved Logistics[/b] update will have:
[list]
[*] Multiple selection for buildings and roads
[*] Updated traffic logistics for oversaturated roads.
[*] Improved way upgrading
[*] Resources will show a thumbnail of the stock graph in the HUD.
[*] Improved storage center functionality
[*] Improved notifications and UI for worker and drone status
[*] Improved space elevator presentation and new animations
[*] Improved special project presentation
[/list]

After that, we have more content updates planned! While we can't share all of the particulars yet, you can have a little sneak peak as a treat. 😊

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/fa7ffb2b3253f1b55464faf396299a20b3f6e272.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/0724c8bfbdf9a8e4e9048c679f18b9f1d7682d9d.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/af5b689062df94c01b6655a300082b79813d6e24.png[/img]

As you can see, later this year we'll begin working on workshop support with our [b]Martian Modding[/b] content update. It's incredibly important for us to make sure that these tools work for our community. To that end, we're looking for modders who would be interested in giving us feedback as we develop our modding tools. If you're interested in joining our early access modding group, please let us know by [url=https://forms.gle/QXVjfiuMw39E18z39]filling out this form here![/url] Past modding experience is preferred, but not necessarily required. 

We're very excited for what's in store! We hope that this roadmap shines a little more light on what's in store for the game and shows that we intend to support this game for the future. We're so grateful to all of our players and for your continued feedback, suggestions, and bug reports.

Ad Astra,
Tlön Industries

notes.title: Per Aspera review - a city builder that's serene yet terrifying
notes.content:
When I begin my terraforming mission on Mars, I am nothing but a voice inside my own head. I have a small base with a few resources and one plucky little worker who's ready to obey my every command. I am AMI, a machine sent to Mars. I have one purpose, one drive, one task: to make Mars habitable for human life.

I can't help but think of Prometheus - the Alien movie no one seems to like - and David the android's complexities, his need to imitate and understand. AMI is the sole entity on Mars, and she speaks to herself through what she understands as 'reflections', making Per Aspera more than a city builder. It's darker, more chilling than it appears at first. I get started on building my base, but there's always something lurking in the back of my mind, like a presence just out of view.

Per Aspera's economy is built on resources and the balancing act of ferrying those resources to different structures as and when they are needed. You start off small, but gradually sweep across craters and unruly terrain, taming Mars into a habitable haven for the incoming humans. AMI may be alone on Mars, but she is not alone - on the other end of a communicator is Doctor Nathan Foster, the scientist that constructed her, and who dubs her the most intelligent machine ever created.

Read the rest of the story...

notes.title: First look at combat
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/ac5c65f87cdd2134221a55e286e28490ddca768c.png[/img]

As your colony grows and your reach expands, you'll discover looming menances and mysterious combatants. You'll need to defend your colonists by researching military tech and building an army of assault drones. In this blog and in the video below, we reveal a quick overview of the combat in Per Aspera!

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z3sQl2I7_vw

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/79469fe456631f15e09e693dfb3d736566c996d1.gif[/img]
[i]Enemy assault drone forces beginning to congregate at two drone hives![/i]

Once you uncover an enemy base, you'll need to pause your terraforming efforts and redirect your energy towards managing this new threat. These forces may seem puny to begin with, but without any defenses of your own, they'll make short work of your base. To avoid watching your colonists' and base's demise, you can begin researching a new branch in the technology tree: Military.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/29ff810d79743b60aba018a69ec9b9ddd2bb596a.jpg[/img]
[i]The beginning of the Military technology tree.[/i]

The Military technology tree has several different paths and upgrades available for you to prioritize. You can focus on increasing your production by prioritizing research into more efficient assault drone factories. You can build better defensives by researching improved drone hives or building better shields for your assault drones. You can also increase your overall drone capacity or augment your assault drones' weapons and speed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/34189eb2eb974f7636897668585a37ab35450ff6.gif[/img]
[i]A group of one hundred assault drones stationed in their drone hive, vigilantly protecting our colony.[/i]

Whichever route you decide, you'll need to get started by building at least two crucial buildings. First, you'll need to build an assault drone factory to produce your units. Next, you'll need to construct a hive. The drone hives serve two purposes: they house your assault drones and also serve as a defensive bastion for your surrounding buildings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/dd2e0a482538ebfaa0740d8c5c684670c693f1d8.gif[/img]
[i]Our combined forces handily crushing the enemy drones and destroying their solar farms.[/i]

After you've finished manufacturing your assault drones, you're nearly ready to begin the attack. Gather together your forces and decide on a strategy. Will you focus on crushing the enemy's power sources or prioritize nullifying their assault drones? Do you prefer to play defensively or love sabotaging the enemy's production with quick, decisive skirmishes? 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/4c40e3dc9427d58af3c2461c3516745e871ad63e.gif[/img]
[i]The combat lens demonstrating where our force's current targets are and whether there are any approaching enemy drones.[/i]

The combat lens is key to prioritizing and identifying threats. Whether you're staging your forces before an attack or making tough decisions during the heat of the battle, you'll want to frequently consult this lens. Using the combat lens can help you quickly establish where your forces are stationed or where they're currently en route to. The combat lens can also help you locate your enemy's forces and even see if they're on the move.

Once the enemy's drone forces have been forcibly deactivated, you may be tempted to leave. That would be a mistake, however -- you'd find that the enemy base will begin to repair and rebuild the damage done. It's important to clear out the rest of the base whenever possible to prevent them from building back up. Once the enemy has been completely eradicated, you'll be able to move your own colony in and claim those precious resources as your own!

notes.title: The five stages of terraforming
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/0d56028fe5bfd060a17ba642dc47e75bf418aa8c.png[/img]

The quest to terraform Mars for human habitation will be complex and difficult. Remember that this isn’t the first time this mission has been attempted! As you explore Mars, you’ll discover countless failed attempts scattered throughout the surface of the Red Planet. We’ve divided the terraforming process into five distinct stages, each with their own unique challenges, innovative projects, and rewards:
[olist]
[*]Sublimating the dry ice poles
[*]Creating an atmosphere
[*]Ecopoiesis
[*]Green Mars
[*]Breathable Atmosphere
[/olist]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/141f51df829154cdfe38e465aa512ec82d5c18bd.gif[/img]

Once you establish your base and welcome your first colonists to their new home, you’ll need to begin the first stage of the terraforming process: melting the poles. Why is that the beginning of your journey to terraform a new home? Mars’s ice poles contain an immense amount of CO₂. Releasing these gases are necessary to warm the climate: they’ll trap heat and trigger a runaway greenhouse effect!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/991f08440173b6a4ecbbbc4e37608f31e400be66.gif[/img]
[i]A ring of greenhouse gas factories and biodomes working to terraform Mars![/i]

Once the poles are sublimated, the next step is to create an atmosphere that increases pressure and aids rising temperatures. There will be many different ways to accomplish this: one example is by building greenhouse gas factories that free the CO₂ trapped in Mars’s regolith.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/3b759a2c2269e1d41883e64c4bfedd3ead8b4dba.png[/img]
[i]J.M Graham’s mountain model for ecosynthesis on Mars.[/i]

The next three stages involve introducing oxygen into the environment and eventually balancing the planet’s overall CO₂ and O₂ levels. [u][url=http://baby.indstate.edu/asgsb/bulletins/v19n2/105%20-%20120%20Graham.pdf]“Planetary Ecosynthesis as Ecological Succession.”[/url][/u] by J.M Graham explains these stages elegantly by comparing ecosynthesis to a mountain descent. “The present climate of Mars can be compared to a very high mountain on Earth, one higher than any real mountain that exists in fact. The prebiotic stage of ecosynthesis employs planetary engineering techniques to bring the climate of Mars at some latitudes into the range of that in the terrestrial Dry Valleys of Antarctica. At that point the introduction of the first microbial ecosystems can begin. Continued modification of the planetary climate will permit the introduction of a sequence of ecosystems from tundra through boreal forests to temperate ecosystems.”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/d05aadeae0f140cd9b31061a915dc3057fc9ac90.gif[/img]
[i]An aquadome slowly propagating bioengineered cyanobacteria over time into an ocean.[/i]

In other words, once Mars’s climate becomes similar to an Earth polar desert, we can begin to introduce extremophile life forms. These microbial ecosystems will begin to slowly convert CO₂ into much needed oxygen. Present-day scientists are currently experimenting to see whether bioengineered extremophiles can survive on (and even modify!) Mars’s harsh environment. By creating a simulated engineered Martian environment, scientists tested five genera of cyanobacteria and three eubacterial strains. Based on preliminary results, some specific extremophiles [b]can[/b] survive! You can read more in this absolutely fascinating paper: [u][url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/228653470_Extremophiles_for_ecopoiesis_desirable_traits_for_and_survivability_of_pioneer_Martian_organisms]“Extremophiles for ecopoiesis: desirable traits for and survivability of pioneer Martian organisms”[/url][/u] by Thomas, Boling, Boston, Campbell, McSpadden, McWilliams, and Todd. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/ca840389f0397f7b545d78accdc258b2a62457b5.gif[/img]
[i]An airship full of colonists travelling to a Martian research outpost over a blue lake![/i]

By building aquadomes and biodomes in Per Aspera, you’ll begin to spawn cyanobacteria, lichens, and green algae across Mars. Eventually as you progress further down the proverbial mountain, continue to research innovative biotech, and get closer to fulfilling the dream of a habitable Mars, your planet will be able to support more advanced lifeforms. Your biodomes and aquadomes will then begin to introduce genetically modified plants and eventually even animals!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/e9f7730c1df47b25e8bbaadc0b709d60db008179.gif[/img]
[i]This is fine.[/i]

In the final stages of terraforming, it will be incredibly important to control your levels of oxygen, limit your CO₂ to 5% or lower, and to introduce nitrogen into your atmosphere. All of these carefully combined will allow humans and animals to naturally breathe on Mars sans any gear! While simple in theory, this balance will be tricky to achieve. If you allow your oxygen levels to surpass 30%, you may personally discover that high levels of oxygen are incredibly flammable. Work quickly to get it under control or run the risk of watching your colony burn down. 

Another important part of this stage is reducing radiation. Once your space elevator is complete, you’ll be able to launch a special project designed to tackle this problem: the magnetic dipole shield. Launching this large dipole in L1 (between Mars and the sun) leaves Mars in a safe magnetotail and stops the stripping of the atmosphere. You can learn more in the talk [u][url=https://livestream.com/viewnow/vision2050/videos/150701155]“A Future Mars Environment for Science and Exploration”[/url][/u] which begins at the 1 hour and 36 minute mark.

notes.title: Special projects & the orbital view
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/3b3c476899c85299c3695d76412c8cefdb27988d.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/2446e1b1dcf9bedd3ac7efa5ff8ba5c02ffd792a.gif[/img]
[i]A newly built spaceport blasting off.[/i]

Once you get your base’s foundation established on Mars, your first order of business will be to begin interplanetary travel by building a spaceport! Once your spaceport is complete, you’ll no longer be restricted to building on the Martian ground… you’ll unlock the Orbital View! This view will allow AMI to undertake special space projects - the first special project begins the migration process and concludes with welcoming your first colonists. As your colony grows and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/newshub/app/803050/view/2933494053297640595]your research uncovers new discoveries,[/url] new special projects will become available!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/5ee4b62a88715174d93e76639005bcd055b246ec.jpg[/img]
[i]A few of the different projects in the orbital view![/i]

Your number of operational spaceports determines how many projects you can work on at once. Some projects are ongoing -- for example, if you have the space for them, you can continue to welcome new colonists to Mars indefinitely by continuing the migration project. Other projects are limited to a single time such as repairing a damaged satellite... or crashing Deimos into Mars. Some things you can only do once; there's only one Deimos after all!

 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/ec7abe10d278b9ec763015119485335f542c15a2.gif[/img]
[i]Building a new foothold by launching an additional landing site.[/i]

When you begin the game, you’ll have a single landing site and a small amount of materials to get your base started. You’ll begin in the Syrtis Major Planum and be restricted to Sector 4. But from humble beginnings come great things: eventually your colony will [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/803050/announcements/detail/4692147266520827527]stretch across the entire planet and become a true ecumenopolis.[/url] In order to grow your colony, you’ll use special projects to expand AMI’s operational reach. By launching satellites, new sectors are unlocked and available for AMI to explore and build into. You can slowly snake along the planet and expand your colony into these new sectors… or you can launch a new foothold entirely by building an additional landing site!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/844073ce8e1cf240545e5b1a87d9bdc1e2a00858.gif[/img]
[i]Melting the poles to create an ocean... with nukes![/i]

While these are the basic special projects, eventually you’ll be able to implement bleeding edge scientific advancements. Remember that your main directive is to terraform Mars; to transform it into a verdant paradise deserving of humanity’s second home. In order to accomplish that unbelievable feat, you may be tempted to resort to extreme measures that have never been seriously attempted before: like nuking the poles to create oceans, crashing Deimos into the surface of Mars, or building an orbital mirror array via a space elevator. You can also try less extreme options such as importing excess greenhouse gases from Earth or building a fleet of cargo ships to bring your colony ice from Europa or nitrogen from Titan.

notes.title: Defining the future: designing our tech tree
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/fcb6033b7dc564adf908d7338553e7df836c7065.png[/img]

Among the colonists who have left Earth for an intrepid life on Mars are the world’s best scientists, engineers, and doctors. Once your first colonists arrive, they will immediately get to work doing what they do best: research. Your colonist’s discoveries and inventions will go a long way towards helping to transform Mars into a new home for humanity.

But as the world’s first super-intelligent Artificial Consciousness, you may be wondering... why would AMI even need colonists to perform research? The ISA built this in as a fail-safe mechanism in order to prevent AMI from reaching the Singularity. In short, it’s a symbiotic relationship: you need the colonists and the colonists need you.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/b3974daee14f1b9de3de9451965e844783a7609c.jpg[/img]
[i]The beginning of the Technology Tree in-game.[/i]

The tech tree is where you can direct your colonist’s efforts and select new upgrades for your colony. As you complete projects and discover new technology, your base will be able to grow to new heights by utilizing bleeding-edge sciences. Build a hyperloop to transport materials and workers across the planet at lightning speeds, discover new ways to provide efficient power, and much more!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/d0192264c8262d3181f38e054c5a719f33dc8f5c.gif[/img]
[i]A newly completed hyperloop for optimal interplanet transport.[/i]

It’s difficult to predict where the world will actually be in 100 years. We’ve dug through a myriad of talks and papers to get a sense of where we’re heading according the leading experts. [url=https://www.amazon.com/dp/B004WNAA88/ref=dp-kindle-redirect?_encoding=UTF8&btkr=1]“Physics of the Future” by Dr. Michio Kaku[/url] was particularly interesting to read! Here's one quote from the book: “‎By 2100, our destiny is to become like the gods we once worshipped and feared. But [b]our tools will not be magic wands and potions but the science of computers, nanotechnology, artificial intelligence,[/b] biotechnology, and most of all, the quantum theory.”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/ea252bcd77ce8336612ad07d141443b01386e103.gif[/img]
[i][url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5qqsMjy8Rx0]The Perseverance[/url] in 2020...[/i]

Humanity has gazed upon Mars in fascination and wonder across the ages. The surface of the Red Planet is covered with those past forgotten missions. As your colony grows, you’ll find old friends like the Perseverance and Pathfinder! We’ve included all of the present-day Martian missions in the game and placed them using their projected destinations. We’ve also imagined future missions that we've added  into the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/9ec4c91b1d9463ec92ae09efbe53a5c79ddb5691.gif[/img]
[i]...And the Perseverance much, much later! Building a Research Outpost on the Perseverance’s location in-game![/i]

This isn’t the first time the mission to colonize Mars has been attempted… but you can use those past failures to prepare for a better future. Once you discover a past mission or failed colony, you can build a research outpost that allows your colonists to survey the area. Research outposts boost your colony’s science production and may also uncover just the thing you need for a scientific breakthrough! After completing their survey, your researchers will send along a report that tells you what exactly they found in the ruins. Discover forgotten secrets, learn from the past, and secure your colony’s future.

notes.title: Sci-fi colony builder Per Aspera will let you try to terraform Mars (again) this December
notes.content:
Despite the fact that we haven't actually been back to the Moon since 1972, that hasn't stopped humanity's imagination from stretching further. Our own local space is not enough - we must go to Mars!

Sci-fi city/colony builder Per Aspera is one such symptom of this recent fascination with the Red Planet. You play as AMI, an artificial intelligence housed in a command and control satellite above Mars, and your role is to embark upon a decades-long journey to slowly terraform the planet for human habitation. Our own Gina Lees had a mess around with a preview build not so long ago, but it won't be long before you can try it out for yourself. Per Aspera will be released on PC via Steam and GOG.com on December 3.

The early game is reminiscent of Paradox Interactive's similar city builder game, Surviving Mars, and much of the start will be about harvesting resources with robot workers and getting the initial colonies set-up so that real people can come live in metal domes. But you'll always be working towards the eventual end goal of giving the planet a breathable atmosphere, one way or another.

[i]Did you know? You can see AMI in our key art! This satellite that orbits Mars houses their "physical body."[/i]

AMI is the artificial consciousness tasked with directing the Martian terraforming initiative that will transform humanity into an interplanetary species. They are who you will play as in Per Aspera. We're so excited to reveal that the wonderful [b]Laila Berzins[/b] stars as AMI! Laila's breadth of performance has been a joy for the dev team and we love how she brings AMI's journey to life.

 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/3cc67259ea48ed58293174b3c0daf89f8541f7ab.gif[/img]

This isn't the first time this mission has been attempted; despite humanity's fascination with Mars, none of the previous missions have been successful. Considering the string of failures... this is humanity's last chance to colonize Mars. The International Space Agency's chief robonaut engineer, Dr. Nathan Foster, developed a revolutionary idea: to send an advanced and autonomous AI to direct the mission. [b]You are this AI[/b] and this new approach will make all the difference.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/c1ede67f2db7d8c824cfb67fb4737da686e5fd21.gif[/img]
[i]"Mars is littered with abandoned missions. I have to focus on my own mission, so we don't turn out like one of those." -AMI[/i]

AMI is a fledgling, autonomous AI.  As an artificial consciousness, AMI was built to constantly analyze the world and discuss philosophical viewpoints with themselves. Life on Mars will present tough choices that forge or test relationships and impact how your mission concludes. The colonists will look to you for survival and you will need to adapt to survive. These new experiences will spark AMI's evolution and growth.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/e12d0551cf3cde8226c48bd7cf2cfe974d632600.gif[/img]

notes.title: Per Aspera has you tame Mars with cute little robots
notes.content:
Per Aspera is a charming little city builder wrapped in a gargantuan strategy game. Its vast scope encompasses such intricate details as small cargo holds and worker stations, yet your playground is the entirety of the surface of Mars. Its charm is sometimes at odds with its scope - perhaps it's more twee than it intends to be - but it certainly delivers the anticipation and awe of discovering, settling, and surviving a new frontier.

Part of that is surely its authenticity. Mars's topography is based on geographical data from NASA, and my mission - as an AI tasked with preparing Mars for human habitation - draws upon scientific studies and theories proposed by real space agencies and engineers.

Later in the game, you'll see blue oceans fill in the lower elevations of the surface as you reach the terraforming stage, but here at the start of my mission, I begin with only a landing site, a small pile of resources, and one robotic worker. I'm a little adrift - the controls aren't as intuitive as I need them to be - but the tutorial does a good job of giving me small objectives to build a base. And, after a bit of poking around the UI to figure out how, I'm soon producing my own iron, carbon, and chemicals, my little worker dutifully ferrying them to where they need to be.

Read the rest of the story...

notes.title: Designing our key art: a Martian ecumenopolis
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/f7a90e9a797bfa0edd6f51b5ae1ff51d3df03775.png[/img]

You see it nearly everywhere Per Aspera is… now it's time to dive into how we made it. In this week's devlog we'll show you the inspirations, mock ups, and philosophy behind our gorgeous key art. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/ef9cdb01201b12c70e2d3cac7bf4ad7d1107534f.gif[/img]
[i]Arriving on Coruscant, the planet-sized city (Star Wars: The Phantom Menace)[/i]

Our game is a strategic simulator with a planet-sized twist. From Star War's Coruscant, Warhammer 40k's Holy Terra, and even Isaac Asimov's Trantor... the [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecumenopolis]ecumenopolis[/url] has captivated science fiction’s imagination since the ‘40s. The idea of creating a city that engulfs Mars and can be seen from orbit is crucial to Per Aspera's premise. That's why we chose to create a Martian ecumenopolis for our key art.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/970a64a426bc33b7c7a5bb92c49187c56a737294.png[/img]
[i]An early mock up sketch showing the terraforming process and urban sprawl![/i]

The goal of terraforming Mars into a lush paradise whilst maintaining an ever-growing urban sprawl is the crux of our game. You can see in this early draft how we show these two contrasting ideas in red, green, and gray. In this beginning mock up, the sprawl's exponential growth is beginning to encroach and conquer the newly-terraformed green pastures.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/8d1ef1456c2ae4b40f984ff3d9353bdf382f392c.png[/img]
[i]Early in-game HUD references from the orbital view.[/i]

Another key part of Per Aspera is [i]who[/i] you play as... an artificial consciousness named AMI. AMI is in charge of helming the terraforming directive for years and generations to come. To represent AMI's unique perspective, we considered how an artificial consciousness would interpret Mars's transformation. The idea was to visualize the orbital data and information being constantly calculated by AMI via HUD elements.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/8fa7be7cf17167555deead47725c9e310bb1fa19.png[/img]
[i]AMI’s satellite in orbit around Mars.[/i]

We also made sure to include AMI's "body" in the key art. That satellite orbiting Mars is where AMI's quantum processing unit and memory storage, just to name a few things, is physically located!

notes.title: Rush hour on Mars
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/b905b1802fe5129d8dd2960f24870d6a7bc04ffe.png[/img]

As your colony grows to stretch across the red expanse of Mars, newly built roads will expand your reach and workers will diligently travel to and fro building, scrapping, and transporting materials. Each time your base expands, you’ll need more roads and eventually even more workers to keep everything working perfectly. While the worker hub acts as your worker’s base of operations, you’ll find that the service area limit isn’t strict. Sometimes your workers will cross the boundary to grab or deposit a tantalizing resource that’s on the other side. This can help in unique cases where you need just a little extra help before setting up a new worker hub. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/40147ef6de0e60ac5f37decc2cb75784052aa38b.gif[/img]

In Per Aspera, efficiency is paramount! To keep your colony running at top efficiency, use the traffic lens to identify which areas of your base need improvements or restructuring. This Lens will allow you to analyze how heavily loaded each Worker Hub is. The load is calculated with a combination of factors, the most important ones being the total time the worker is working (vs at rest) and the amount of pending cargo that is waiting to be ferried across to an area. If an area is heavily loaded, you will need to consider adding more Worker Hubs and partition your base in a more efficient manner. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/7b8d1b2dba072770353b997db50cb0bec1f498a1.gif[/img]

You won’t want to have too many traffic jams on Mars! The traffic lens will also let you take a look at the individual saturation of each and every road and hyperloop. Keep an eye open to detect bottlenecks in the roads, as they are ideal candidates for upgrades. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/c360004d73a47d6c8edd0d95d440598e48a47852.gif[/img]

As your colony grows, you may find that you’ve created a veritable urban sprawl and that it’s hard to focus on certain aspects. The traffic lens was designed to help you quickly determine how the roads and workers, which are the foundational building blocks of your colony, are operating. We were inspired by the different tools city planners use to determine efficiency and density such as [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isochrone_map]isochrone maps[/url] and [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4h60oC5-Y6A]traffic heatmaps.[/url]

[i]This is an example of a traffic heatmap analyzing rush hour in a metropolitan area.[/i]

notes.title: Meet your workers
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/47479beb2ce693d0d15e9cbf60267d5898a988b9.png[/img]

Workers are your arms and legs on the cold surface of Mars. They are unmanned rovers that shuttle resources around your base and also handle the construction and eventual scrapping of buildings. Even though they move autonomously, they are an extension of your own self. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/2904deca2898f3427dca6f6e0b4a62a758e89986.gif[/img]

You begin with a single worker -- it's equipped with construction drones that can 3D print entire buildings. Each worker requires a hub to operate from: they’ll use the hub to store materials and service the surrounding area. The Landing Site and Worker Hub both serve as centers for workers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/51c23a9592f313fbccf050aea3ba49a833c5be88.png[/img]
[i]Early concept sketches of the trusty worker![/i]

When we started working on the game, we knew we wanted our workers to replicate the kind of experience The Settlers had. While the little serfs in that game live on the roads, we’ve decided for our workers to live in buildings so they can be protected from inclement Mars weather. After experimenting quite a lot, we found it felt best to add a special building specifically for workers! That’s how we designed the Worker Hub.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/072cc10f1107b6f39ed5d03e234fb844c7ea3504.gif[/img]

Workers are built automatically in Worker Factories as long as there are vacant hubs. You'll need to build many replacements since workers have such a tough life: the harsh Martian climate and solar radiation eventually causes irreparable decay. That’s why it’s important to have factories that constantly create fresh, new workers. In a way, we were loosely inspired by [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-replicating_spacecraft#:~:text=self%2Dreplicating%20nature.-,Von%20Neumann%20probes,to%20explore%20or%20examine%20something).]Von Neumann probes[/url] -- self-sufficient constructs that can build self-replicating bases or even copies of themselves. While you start Mars with only a single yet capable worker, by the end of the game you’ll command a legion of them!

notes.title: Designing the perfect roads
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/2301ddab71b8297a7baab5f804178dfbef536ede.png[/img]

Roads lie at the core of Per Aspera. A well designed colony is connected seamlessly by a vast network of expanding roads. In our game, it’s very important to plan your building placement carefully! The ultimate directive of AMI is to terraform the planet... but one of the first steps to accomplishing that is by creating efficient resource transportation. That’s precisely where roads come in.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/3aaffe06bcbaadd6ab6706d2c7a5204774021be4.gif[/img]

The foundation of a good colony is an optimized network of roads and buildings connected with Workers. When you begin a new structure, a new road will be created that links it to your pre-existing structures.  Each particular road is calculated on the fly based on the real topology of Mars. The roads will try to minimize the travel time between buildings, as the Workers travel faster the flatter the road is. We modelled the different speeds on a 1985 paper commissioned by the US Department of Transportation called [url=https://deepblue.lib.umich.edu/bitstream/handle/2027.42/137/73427.0001.001.pdf][u]“Methods for Predicting Truck Speed Loss on Grades”[/u][/url] (by Robert Gillespie), adjusted for Mars gravity.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/2558ffef6bdcfa120763a63f3938d0dfac6903cf.gif[/img]

For the curious cats, these animated tendrils are not a visual effect, it’s the actual pathfinding algorithm running in real-time! We implemented an algorithm from a paper by Galin, Peytavie, Maréchal and Guérin called [url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/229707505_Procedural_Generation_of_Roads][u]“Procedural Generation of Roads”,[/u][/url] which consists of a hyperdense A* search on a dynamic lattice. This is a very novel technique designed to be used in real civil engineering road planification. We think Per Aspera must be one of the first games to use such a technique!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/6573b5cf533e5a3f23d90346e220959024a0b112.gif[/img]

We were also inspired by classic games like The Settlers (AKA Serf City: Life is Feudal), which provided hours and hours of optimization fun! We hope our players will have just as much fun planning and optimizing their settlements.

notes.title: Discover Mars at the Indie Arena Booth this weekend
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/fc787a390ef4fe96e37decdafb54a659ccd9eb96.png[/img]

Welcome to your new home: Mars, the red planet. There’s not much there yet… but that’s exactly where you come in. Begin the terraforming journey this weekend -- download our public demo this weekend at the [b]Indie Arena Booth.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/95ad2726245e52c6f37a146ce3566edcceefdb96.gif[/img]

[b]Per Aspera[/b] will be showcasing at [b]Gamescom’s virtual Indie Arena Booth[/b] this week. Join us beginning [b]August 27th until August 30th.[/b] Swing by our virtual booth, check out our gameplay livestreams on Steam, and begin terraforming your new home on Mars by playing the demo. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/e5aba99cd059721adb71ea4ae1fda834db8886fc.png[/img]
[i]Here’s a sneak peak behind the scenes of our virtual booth! 💕[/i][/center]

We’ve been hard at work getting everything ready for the big week. We’re so excited for you to try out the game! This demo focuses on the simulation part of the game: players will begin the long and arduous process of terraforming Mars. Before you set off into the unknown and begin the first step of transforming your new home, let’s review the basics. 

[b][h2]EXPLORE A TRUE TO LIFE MARS[/h2][/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/2ec1813bb09dfecffa5c74d033a9b328cd139b68.gif[/img]

We’ve painstakingly based our simulation of Mars off the real thing. We’ve taken the topographical maps of Mars and put them into the game exactly as they are. Ascend the peak of the staggering Olympus Mons, dive into the depths of the Capri Chasma, or meet old rover friends like Viking1 or Pathfinder. Bask in the wonders of the red planet.

[b][h2]ACQUIRE AND REFINE RESOURCES[/h2][/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/3aaffe06bcbaadd6ab6706d2c7a5204774021be4.gif[/img]

The demo focuses on the first stage of terraforming: exploration, mining, refining, and expansion. In the final game, you’ll build a fleet of workers to serve your prime directive. In the beginning, you’ll have just the one. Use your faithful worker to build your first mine, factory, and solar farm. Once your mine is complete, your worker will begin stockpiling the resource. As your operation grows, you’ll refine your unprocessed minerals into resources that help your colony inch towards paradise such as steel, glass, silicon, and more! 

[b][h2]EXPAND YOUR COLONY AND BALANCE YOUR NEEDS[/h2][/b]
Once your landing site has been properly surveyed and built up, you’ll need to expand! Find new resources with an Areological Scanner. Once you discover new veins and resources, it’ll be time to send out a worker. Eventually, you’ll need to expand your reach by building an additional Worker Hub or perhaps even an extra worker.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/5831c51db27d6231d947143f95f9862419c46470.gif[/img]

Keep an eye on your buildings’ power consumption, maintenance needs, and colony’s resource stockpile. Resources and buildings don’t last forever. Your units will require constant care, attention, and adaptation to survive the rugged environment.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35215160/6573b5cf533e5a3f23d90346e220959024a0b112.gif[/img]

We’re so excited for you to get your first taste of the game! We have been working on this game for years… it’s surreal to think that soon the game will be in your hands. We’ll be looking forward to hearing your thoughts and feedback. In the meantime, stay tuned for later this week!
